use_case_name: Browse and Search Files and Archives

claims.content: Enable PeaZip’s users to browse and gain access, in various ways, to every area of the computer system on which PeaZip runs as well as to included objects (archives and files), and to search in this folder and subfolders or in this folder only.

goal.raw_text: Enable PeaZip’s users to browse and gain access, in various ways, to every area of the computer system on which PeaZip runs as well as to included objects (archives and files), and to search in this folder and subfolders or in this folder only.

claims.content: User
An operating system is present on the computer system.
The user is in the PeaZip file manager interface, which is the initial window of the application.
For browsing an archive, the archive is in a read-only (browsing and extraction) format supported by PeaZip.
If the archive to be browsed is password-protected, the user knows the password and, if there is one, keyfile required to have access to the archive contents for browsing.
The user presses the 'File' button in the initial window of the application (file manager interface), uses the navigation bar, or invokes F3/Ctrl+F3 to browse and search files and archives.

trigger.raw_text: The user presses the 'File' button in the initial window of the application (file manager interface), uses the navigation bar, or invokes F3/Ctrl+F3 to browse and search files and archives.

claims.content: In the initial window of the application (file manager interface), the User presses the “File” button.
A submenu opens with choices that have to do with browsing and access to areas and objects of the computer systems.
The main window, under the “root” directory, shows a table listing disk information, and at the bottom of the window it indicates that the current browsing location is “USER-PC [user]”.
In the initial window of the application (file manager interface), the User presses the “Browser” button.
A submenu opens with choices that have to do with transferring to main interfaces of PeaZip and selecting view mode for objects (archives and files) displayed in file manager interface.
The User selects “Toggle browse/flat view”, which displays all together the objects contained in the current path or in the archive.
The User invokes F3 to perform recursive search (search in this folder and subfolders) or Ctrl+F3 to perform non recursive search (search here).
The User selects “Refresh” or presses F5 to refresh/update of currently displayed content.

At step 2, the User can browse the desktop with F2, browse the user’s home with Ctrl+F2, browse the computer’s root with Shift+F2, or browse the archive root with Ctrl+Shift+F2 if browsing inside an archive (otherwise browse the computer’s root).
At step 2, the User can go to the computer system’s or archive’s root with Ctrl+R.

At step 2, the User can open a directory/archive with < or Enter or double click, go up one level with > or Ctrl+U or click on the blue arrow icon or F4, go back in history with Ctrl+B or Backspace, and go forward in history with Ctrl+F.
At step 2, the User can browse the most recently visited item with F7 or browse the first item in the bookmarks list with F8.
At step 4, the User can select “Go to archiving layout” to lead directly to the create archive interface or “Go to extraction layout” to lead directly to the extraction interface.
At step 5, instead of selecting “Toggle browse/flat view”, the User can toggle browse mode / flat view mode with * or F6.
At step 6, in search/filter mode, the User can go to the object’s path with Ctrl+P.
At step 7, instead of selecting “Refresh” or pressing F5, the User can click the refresh button in the navigation bar.

1. If the User does not know or does not insert the password and (if there is one) keyfile required for an archive, the User cannot have access to the archive’s contents for browsing; browsing of that archive cannot proceed, so this exception exits the browse/search attempt for that archive.
The User has browsed and gained access, in various ways, to every area of the computer system on which PeaZip runs, as well as to included objects (archives and files).
The User has direct access to a path of an object or a file/archive.
The User has searched and gained access to objects they would like to manage.
The objects contained in the current path or in the archive are displayed all together.
Currently displayed content is refreshed/updated.
For an archive requiring a password and (if there is one) keyfile, the User has access to the archives contents for browsing.
